description: A comprehensive study of the net movement of mass from one location, stream or phase to another due to a concentration gradient, encompassing diffusion, distillation, absorption, and extraction processes.

sections.title: Molecular Diffusion
sections.description: The random thermal movement of individual molecules through a fluid due to a concentration gradient, analyzed primarily in stagnant or laminar flow conditions.

equations: Where J_A is the molar flux, D_AB is the mass diffusivity (diffusion coefficient), and (dC_A / dz) is the concentration gradient.

results: Equimolar Counter Diffusion (EMCD): N_A = -N_B. The total molar flux is exactly zero (e.g., diffusion of two gases in a closed tube).
Diffusion of A through Non-diffusing B: N_B = 0. The bulk flow contributes to the flux of A (e.g., evaporation of a liquid into a stagnant gas).

sections.title: Convective Mass Transfer
sections.description: The transfer of mass between a boundary surface and a moving fluid, or between two relatively immiscible moving fluids, characterized by mass transfer coefficients.

equations: N_A = k_c * (C_A1 - C_A2) or N_A = k_g * (p_A1 - p_A2)
Where k_c and k_g are the mass transfer coefficients based on concentration and partial pressure driving forces, respectively.

key_concepts.explanation: Sherwood Number (Sh) represents the ratio of convective to diffusive mass transfer. Schmidt Number (Sc) represents the ratio of momentum diffusivity (kinematic viscosity) to mass diffusivity.

Film Theory assumes mass transfer occurs purely by molecular diffusion through a stagnant film at the interface. Higbie's Penetration Theory assumes fluid eddies arrive at the interface, remain for a fixed contact time, and then return to the bulk fluid.

sections.title: Gas Absorption
sections.description: A unit operation used to remove one or more components from a gas mixture by dissolving them into a liquid solvent.

key_concepts.explanation: For dilute solutions at constant temperature, the equilibrium partial pressure of a gas above a liquid is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid (p_A = H * x_A).

The total height of a packed absorption column (Z) is calculated as Z = NTU * HTU, where NTU is the Number of Transfer Units (indicating the difficulty of separation) and HTU is the Height of a Transfer Unit (indicating equipment efficiency).

results: Loading Point: The gas velocity at which liquid begins to accumulate in the packing, increasing the pressure drop rapidly.
Flooding Point: The maximum allowable gas velocity where liquid fills the entire void space and is blown out the top of the column. Columns are typically operated at 60-80% of the flooding velocity.

sections.title: Distillation
sections.description: A thermal separation process utilized to separate liquid mixtures into their individual components based on significant differences in their volatilities or boiling points.

equations: Where 'y' is the vapor phase mole fraction and 'x' is the liquid phase mole fraction. If alpha_AB = 1, separation by ordinary distillation is absolutely impossible (Azeotrope).

key_concepts.explanation: A graphical method to determine the number of ideal theoretical stages required for a binary distillation. It relies heavily on the assumption of Constant Molar Overflow (CMO).

The ratio of the liquid returned to the column to the distillate product removed (R = L/D). Total Reflux yields the minimum number of stages, while Minimum Reflux requires an infinite number of stages.

sections.title: Extraction and Drying
sections.description: Operations involving the separation of a solute using a liquid solvent (Liquid-Liquid Extraction) and the removal of liquid moisture from a solid via thermal vaporization (Drying).

key_concepts.explanation: The ratio of the concentration of the solute in the extract phase to its concentration in the raffinate phase at thermodynamic equilibrium.

A fundamental plot of drying rate versus free moisture content. It typically features a 'Constant Rate Period' (surface evaporation) and a 'Falling Rate Period' (internal diffusion limited). The boundary between these is the Critical Moisture Content.
